text:
oliver: Weird bug report: users hit `Event loop is closed` when reusing an AsyncClient created during import-time in webapps that use uvloop. Stacktrace points into anyio. Repro below, very intermittent. Has anyone dug into constructor vs first-await binding?

maya: please paste a tiny repro, this is likely loop-affinity.

oliver: gist of it:

```
# app.py (import-time client)
import httpx
client = httpx.AsyncClient()

# handler.py
async def handler(req):
    r = await client.get('https://example.com')
    return r.text
```

oliver: In production it fails only after deploys or when gunicorn spawns workers. Locally sometimes fails with `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` on the `await client.get` line.

ryan: classic: AsyncClient (or its transport) captured an event-loop specific resource at construction time. When the process forks/spawns or when uvloop replaces the loop, the captured reference becomes invalid.

zoe: for DX we should: (1) update quickstart examples so they don't encourage top-level AsyncClient creation, (2) add a debug-mode check in __init__ that warns if there is no running loop or if the loop object seems ephemeral, (3) consider lazy-init of the transport on first use.

maya: lazy-init wins for safety, but needs to be thread-safe and robust when shared across tasks. Implementation idea: set _transport = None in __init__, on first await acquire an asyncio.Lock and initialize transport bound to current loop. Also provide an opt-in param `eager_init=True` to keep old behavior for advanced users.

ryan: another idea: explicitly record construction thread/loop repr and if mismatch detected on first use, raise a clear error explaining the anti-pattern and linking to docs. That helps onboard users faster than cryptic anyio traces.

oliver: QA note: this reproduces more often when the app creates clients during import (sync) and the server worker resets/uvloop changes after fork. I've got a small fuzz harness that flips import vs in-loop creation and runs 1000 iterations, found fail rate ~0.7% on my machine.

qa-bot: added flaky test job: sdk/async-client-affinity-fuzz to CI (owner=zoe, severity=medium)

zoe: I'll draft a docs PR and a small runtime guard in debug mode that logs a clear message if constructor_loop != current_loop on first await (and in debug builds optionally raise). Also will add the lazy-init design doc to the SDK repo.

maya: thanks. We should also update typing docs: if we add `eager_init` param call it `transport_init` with Literal["eager","defer"] for clarity. That plays nicer with typed call sites.

oliver: great, will open an issue: "async client: transport loop-affinity - detect or defer" and include the fuzz harness. I'll attach logs. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
